store.listing.description:
Kopiyka Budget keeps your money on your phone. No account, no server, no ads, no trackers, no subscription. It is free now and it stays free.

Everything you enter belongs to you: export the lot as CSV, as a full JSON backup, or as one ZIP that carries your receipt photos with it. A copy is written to your own iCloud Drive every day, and you can restore from it whenever you want.

Logging is meant to take two taps. The entry sheet opens on a calculator keypad: type the amount, with Category and Tags on the keys beside it, then one tap to add. The same keypad is on your Apple Watch, and Siri can add an entry without opening the app.

WHAT IS IN IT

- Budgets for a category, a folder, a tag or for everything, in a month that starts on your payday rather than on the 1st.
- Several accounts in several currencies (cash, bank, card, savings, investment), with net worth and transfers. Exchange rates come from the European Central Bank, kept day by day, so an old transfer still converts correctly.
- Recurring payments: a subscription posts itself on the day and tells you it did, while the ones whose amount moves around wait for your tap. Kopiyka also spots repeats in your history and offers to make rules from them.
- Categories inside folders, each with its own icon and colour, and tags that can be limited to the categories they make sense for.
- Insights you pick yourself: free to spend, days until salary, savings goals, a payments checklist, subscriptions per year, upcoming payments.
- Trips & Events: name a trip or an event (a birthday, a wedding), give it a budget and its days, and every new expense is tagged and counted against it, in whatever currency you spend, and kept out of your monthly budgets.
- Debts, so you know who owes whom, with a reminder before the due date.
- A category suggested from where you are: buy coffee at the same place twice and the third time it is filled in. Your location never leaves the phone.
- Receipt photos on any entry, backed up beside your data.
- An Apple Watch app with the keypad, today's entries and your budgets: approve pending payments, add a note by voice, and start from a complication or a Control Center control.
- In English and Ukrainian.

BANK NOTIFICATIONS (BETA)

iOS never hands card transactions to an app. What it does allow is a Shortcuts automation: when your bank notifies you about a payment, it passes the notification to Kopiyka, which reads the amount, the shop, the card and the time out of the text on the device, silently, with the app closed. The entry waits in Pending until you approve it, on the phone or on your watch, and what the bank said stays beside it, apart from your own note. Settings walks you through the setup once.

Kopiyka is open source. No analytics, no trackers, no third-party SDKs: nothing is collected and nothing is sent anywhere.

Kopiyka is a record-keeping tool, not financial, tax or investment advice.

store.listing.whatsNew:
Thank you Maks for reading this, you're awesome! Hope everything fine with your spine, let's go get some sandwich nearby!

Siriusia (my cutie cat) sees the future, like your drunk, yet perspective, friend. A new insight takes your own pace, adds every currency into one, and carries it forward: when the savings goal lands, what a home would take, how much a daily coffee costs over ten years. Siriusia is a cat. It is a forecast of a very optimistic cat, not a promise, not advice. Tap her and she spins for free too.

Receipts read themselves. Hold + and the receipt camera finds the paper, takes the picture by itself, and reads the total, the shop, the address and every line. One receipt with dinner and a lamp on it becomes two entries, each in its own category. Receipts in another currency ask which account paid.
I personally don't use it often, but I love the way it works (I wish I had that 10 years ago)

Split with friends. You paid 120 for dinner for three, but only 40 was your dinner, for a wonderful math. Each friend’s share is theirs, not your spending, and their page says what they owe, with Remind for the forgetful and Let it go for the very forgetful.

Biedronka, Lidl, Сільпо, АТБ, Orlen, Uber and hundreds more shops are recognised the first time you pay there, and filed into your category of that kind, whatever you called it. The payment still waits in Pending for your "Yes, sir/madam".

One landlord, two bills: the amount now tells the rent from the service charge.

Recurring payments on a calendar: paid, late and still to come.

Also new: a spending map, three new insights, cards suggested from how you use the app, categories ordered by use or dragged into place, trips and events you can rename, and Undo instead of “Are you sure?”. You were sure, and you're sure, don't disappoint me.

Ready for iPhone Duo: folded or open, everything fits, and Save is always on screen. Why? Who knows, maybe I prepare for the 3rd generation.

Smoother all round: pickers open with the keyboard ready and a shop’s usual categories first, dragging to reorder glides, and a payment in a currency with no exchange rate, like the hryvnia, is converted as soon as a rate turns up.

Every button now answers a tap the moment your finger lands. Even the ones that used to pretend they hadn’t noticed.

I fixed numerous bugs which pissed me off. Hope you've never seen those.
